summary.name: Digisensus Recorder
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source Mac call recorder that captures Zoom, Meet, Teams, FaceTime, WhatsApp and phone calls without a meeting bot, and produces transcripts and AI meeting notes.
use_cases: Recording Zoom, Meet or Teams calls without a notetaker bot
Recording FaceTime, WhatsApp or phone calls on a Mac
Generating transcripts and decisions or action items from calls
Searching and organising past call recordings
Keeping call audio private on your own computer
Feeding call recordings to AI agents via MCP or command line
summary.what_it_does: Digisensus Recorder records audio on a Mac from any app that plays call audio, including Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, FaceTime, WhatsApp, Viber, Telegram and Slack, plus iPhone calls answered through Continuity. With auto-record on, it starts when a call begins and stops when the call ends, and a banner with a Stop button shows recording is active. Transcripts show who said what, and AI summaries list decisions and next steps; transcription can use a Digisensus account, an OpenAI-compatible server (including one on your Mac), or no AI at all. Recordings are saved as Ogg Opus audio in a local folder and are only uploaded if you choose to transcribe. A built-in command-line tool and MCP server let AI agents search, export and summarise recordings, and it is off until enabled.
notable: No meeting bot: records audio on the Mac so no participant appears in the call
Open source under GPL-3.0 and can be pointed at your own transcription server
Built-in MCP server and command-line tool for AI agents, off by default
Records audio only and keeps recordings on the Mac as Ogg Opus files
caveats: Requires macOS 15 Sequoia or later and Apple silicon (M1 or newer); no Windows or mobile app
Transcripts and summaries through a Digisensus account come with free daily credit; beyond that, own AI service is needed
Recording laws vary, and informing participants or getting consent is the user's responsibility
